title: Discover, price and protect: turning dashboards into paid work

say: Discover, price and protect: turning dashboards into paid work.
This is the video for module three of Power BI and Tableau: consulting, pricing and your dashboard career.
Technical skill gets a dashboard built. Consulting skill gets it used and paid for.
Most dashboard projects that fail do so before any chart is built.

say: Plan 45 to 60 minutes, take notes, and cover five areas.
Decisions. What will this dashboard help you decide? A dashboard that changes no decision will be abandoned.

panel.heading: Five areas to cover every time
items: Decisions: what will this help you decide?
Audience: who views it, how often, what device?
Data sources: where does each number live?
Refresh: monthly, weekly or daily?
Access and privacy: who may see what?

say: Publish to web in Power BI, and Tableau Public, make your work visible to anyone. Use them for public data only, never for client or staff data.

cards.d: Publish to web and Tableau Public are for public data only. Never use them for client or staff data.
Shows each viewer only their own rows, but only when shared through the service, not in an emailed file.
Collect only the columns you need, mask names and phones, protect devices, delete copies at the end.

say: Row-level security lets one dashboard show each viewer only their own rows, such as a coordinator seeing only her state. It works only when shared through the service, not on a file you email.

say: The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 sets duties for anyone handling personal data. Collect only what you need, mask names and phone numbers, protect your devices, and delete copies when the project ends.
Never send logins or data exports over open WhatsApp groups.

say: For example, Chioma is quoting a two-page sales dashboard. She breaks it into phases. Discovery takes 4 hours. Data access and cleaning takes 16.

Data access and cleaning: 16 hours
Model and measures: 10 hours
Two pages and phone layout: 12 hours
QA and reconciliation: 6 hours
Training and handover: 4 hours

say: The model and measures take 10 hours, and building two pages with a phone layout takes 12.

say: Quality checks take 6 hours, and training and handover 4. That is 52 hours in total.
Notice that cleaning is about 31% of the effort. Explain that to the client, and keep a record of actual hours so your next estimate improves.

panel.rule: Data cleaning is usually the biggest phase. Add contingency.

say: Now she prices it. Her rate of 15,000 naira per hour is for illustration only, not a market rate.
52 hours gives a base price of 780,000 naira. She adds 15% contingency for unknown data problems, 117,000 naira, making 897,000.
She rounds to a fixed 900,000 naira for the defined scope.
Her payment plan is 450,000 naira deposit before starting, 270,000 when the first draft is approved, and 180,000 on handover.
Protect your money. Take a deposit before starting, and receive payment through a traceable channel such as a bank transfer.
Be wary of overseas clients who send too much and ask for a refund of the difference. That is a common scam. Never share banking passwords or one-time codes.
And when the client asks for more, check the written scope and send a priced change request.

panel.heading: Protect your payment
items: Take a deposit before starting
Get paid through a traceable channel
Beware overpayment refund scams
Never share passwords or one-time codes
Price every extra request as a change

say: To remember. Cover all five discovery areas. Use public tools only for public data. Estimate by phase and add contingency.
Build three portfolio projects, each with a short case study of your decisions and checks, and never use client data in them.
